root_cause.text: In the IPv6 TCP listen path for v4-mapped connections, tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() initialized the child socket’s IPv6 state (notably newinet->pinet6 and copied ipv6_pinfo) only after tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() had already inserted the child into the TCP ehash, creating a race where other CPUs could access a partially initialized socket still pointing at the listener’s ipv6_pinfo.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “After tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), the child socket is already visible from TCP ehash table and other cpus might use it” and “newinet->pinet6 is still pointing to the listener ipv6_pinfo”; the patch fixes this by adding opt_child_init and moving that setup into tcp_v6_mapped_child_init(), which is called inside tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() before ehash insertion.

consistency_review.core_intent: Propagate an optional child-socket initialization callback through the SYN-receive child socket creation interfaces across inet/tcp/subflow/SMC paths for compatibility and future custom socket setup.

Extend the syn_recv_sock child-socket creation path to propagate and invoke an optional child initialization hook, updating all relevant callers and IPv4/IPv6 child socket setup to preserve correct option state.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a child-socket initialization hook into the SYN-recv child creation path, including tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), which is the path implicated by the race. This directly supports performing required per-child initialization before or during insertion-sensitive socket setup, matching the root cause of late IPv6 child initialization for v4-mapped connections.

The changes add and propagate a child-socket initialization hook specifically so IPv6-mapped child sockets can be initialized during SYN-recv socket creation, including explicit IPv6 child setup in the IPv4/IPv6 path. That directly addresses the root cause of partially initialized IPv6 state being exposed after ehash insertion.

This change updates the call site for syn_recv_sock() to match the new child-socket creation API introduced by the fix. Although it only passes NULL, it is directly tied to the corrected initialization path for child socket creation and thus is part of the vulnerability-related change set.

The refactor changes the IPv4-mapped IPv6 child socket initialization path in tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() to use a callback during tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), directly affecting when IPv6 state is set relative to ehash insertion—the core race in the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This call creates the child via the IPv4 path, which inserts it into the TCP ehash before the IPv6-specific child state is initialized for v4-mapped sockets, directly enabling the race.
This IPv6-state pointer setup occurs only after the child socket has already been created by tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), leaving a window where other CPUs can observe partially initialized IPv6 state.
The child's ipv6_pinfo is copied from the listener only after the IPv4 child creation path returns, meaning concurrent access can occur before the child gets its own proper IPv6 state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call routes v4-mapped IPv6 child creation through the IPv4 SYN-RECV path, which inserts the child socket into the TCP ehash before the IPv6-specific state is initialized. That ordering is the core race described in the root cause.

This initializes the child socket's IPv6 state pointer only after the child has already been created and exposed via the earlier IPv4 path, leaving a window where other CPUs can observe an incompletely initialized socket.

This copies the listener's IPv6 per-socket state into the child only after the child may already be visible to concurrent lookups, contributing to the race where the child still effectively reflects listener IPv6 state during exposure.
